newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ FUTURES END SHARPLY UP IN TECHNICAL RALLY.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ FUTURES END SHARPLY UP IN TECHNICAL RALLY.

text.p: FCOJ futures ended sharply higher on Monday in the fourth consecutive day of a technically-driven buying spree, dealers said.
Speculative and commission house buying pushed the benchmark September contract through its overhead targets of 78.00 cents and then 80.00 cents a lb in early activity.
Trade scale-up selling stalled gains along the way but did not block the September contract from reaching an eight-week high of 82.25 cents ahead of the close.
Market sources pegged the next upside target at 82.45 cents, the high reached on June 12, followed by 83.00 cents.
"The trade needs to sell into this rally but is letting it come to them," a juice broker said.

September juice finished 4.45 cents firmer at 81.85 cents a lb, having ranged from 82.25 to 77.75 cents. Second-month November rose 4.55 cents on the day to 83.90 cents. The rest of the board ended 3.75 to 4.55 cents higher.

Today's close well above last week's high of 80.25 cents is expected to attract additional buying on Tuesday, traders said. But in the longer term, the outlook remains negative for prices amid a bearish supply and demand picture.

A private estimate of the 1997/98 Florida crop by Citrus Consulting International is expected to reinforce expectations for another record crop in the 1997/98 season. The estimate will be issued on August 14.
An estimated 6,000 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Friday's official 3,176 lots.
